These exercises practise the ideas from Chapter 3: the pipe, the dplyr verbs, reshaping, joins, and cleaning. The first run on this page takes a little longer, because your browser downloads the dplyr and tidyr packages. Where you see `______`, replace it with your own code.


::: {.cell setup='true' exercise='["ex1","ex2","ex3","ex4","ex5","ex6","ex7"]'}
```{webr}
#| setup: true
#| exercise: [ex1, ex2, ex3, ex4, ex5, ex6, ex7]
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
students  <- read.csv("students.csv")
semesters <- read.csv("semesters.csv")
```
:::


## The pipe and the verbs

### Exercise 1: Rewrite with the pipe

Rewrite `round(mean(c(6.5, 7, 5.5, 8, 6)), 1)` using `|>`, so that it reads in the order the steps happen.


::: {.cell exercise='ex1'}
```{webr}
#| exercise: ex1
c(6.5, 7, 5.5, 8, 6) |> ______ |> ______
```
:::


::: { .solution exercise="ex1" }
::: { .callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

```r
c(6.5, 7, 5.5, 8, 6) |> mean() |> round(1)
```
:::
:::

### Exercise 2: Average age by faculty

Find the average age of students in each faculty, sorted from oldest to youngest.


::: {.cell exercise='ex2'}
```{webr}
#| exercise: ex2
students |>
  summarise(mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE), .by = ______) |>
  arrange(______)
```
:::


::: { .hint exercise="ex2" }
::: { .callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint

Group by `faculty`, and sort with `desc(mean_age)` for oldest first.
:::
:::

::: { .solution exercise="ex2" }
::: { .callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

```r
students |>
  summarise(mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE), .by = faculty) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_age))
```
:::
:::

### Exercise 3: Categories with `case_when()`

Add a column `sleep_group`: `"Short"` under 6 hours, `"Recommended"` at 7 hours or more, and `"Moderate"` otherwise. Then count the semester records in each group.


::: {.cell exercise='ex3'}
```{webr}
#| exercise: ex3
semesters |>
  mutate(sleep_group = case_when(
    sleep_hours < 6 ~ "Short",
    ______ ~ "Recommended",
    .default = ______
  )) |>
  count(sleep_group)
```
:::


::: { .hint exercise="ex3" }
::: { .callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint

The second condition is `sleep_hours >= 7`, and `.default` gives the label for everything else.
:::
:::

::: { .solution exercise="ex3" }
::: { .callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

```r
semesters |>
  mutate(sleep_group = case_when(
    sleep_hours < 6 ~ "Short",
    sleep_hours >= 7 ~ "Recommended",
    .default = "Moderate"
  )) |>
  count(sleep_group)
```

Records with missing sleep fall through to `.default`, so they are counted as `"Moderate"` here. To keep them separate, add `is.na(sleep_hours) ~ NA` as the first condition.
:::
:::

## Reshaping and joining

### Exercise 4: One column per semester

Make a table of each student's GPA with one column per semester. Show the first rows.


::: {.cell exercise='ex4'}
```{webr}
#| exercise: ex4
semesters |>
  select(student_id, semester, gpa) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = ______, values_from = ______) |>
  head()
```
:::


::: { .solution exercise="ex4" }
::: { .callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

```r
semesters |>
  select(student_id, semester, gpa) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = semester, values_from = gpa) |>
  head()
```
:::
:::

### Exercise 5: Joining two tables

Join `semesters` to `students` and compare the average semester GPA of full-time and part-time students.


::: {.cell exercise='ex5'}
```{webr}
#| exercise: ex5
semesters |>
  left_join(students, join_by(______)) |>
  summarise(mean_gpa = mean(gpa, na.rm = TRUE), .by = ______)
```
:::


::: { .solution exercise="ex5" }
::: { .callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

```r
semesters |>
  left_join(students, join_by(student_id)) |>
  summarise(mean_gpa = mean(gpa, na.rm = TRUE), .by = study_mode)
```
:::
:::

### Exercise 6: Who left the study?

Use `anti_join()` to find the students with no record for semester 4. How many are there?


::: {.cell exercise='ex6'}
```{webr}
#| exercise: ex6
students |>
  anti_join(semesters |> filter(semester == ______), join_by(student_id)) |>
  nrow()
```
:::


::: { .solution exercise="ex6" }
::: { .callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

```r
students |>
  anti_join(semesters |> filter(semester == 4), join_by(student_id)) |>
  nrow()
```

The same students are missing from semesters 3 and 4: they left after the first year.
:::
:::

## Cleaning

### Exercise 7: A small messy table

This table mimics a survey export. Clean it so that `gender` has only `"Female"` and `"Male"`, and `stress` is a number with the missing code `99` turned into `NA`. Then calculate the average stress.


::: {.cell exercise='ex7'}
```{webr}
#| exercise: ex7
messy <- tibble(
  gender = c("F", "female", "Male", "m", "Female"),
  stress = c("3", "99", "4", "2", "5")
)
clean <- messy |>
  mutate(
    gender = if_else(startsWith(tolower(gender), "f"), ______, ______),
    stress = as.integer(na_if(stress, ______))
  )
clean
mean(clean$stress, na.rm = TRUE)
```
:::


::: { .hint exercise="ex7" }
::: { .callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint

`if_else(condition, value if TRUE, value if FALSE)`. The missing code is the text `"99"`, in quotes, because the column is still text at that point.
:::
:::

::: { .solution exercise="ex7" }
::: { .callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

```r
clean <- messy |>
  mutate(
    gender = if_else(startsWith(tolower(gender), "f"), "Female", "Male"),
    stress = as.integer(na_if(stress, "99"))
  )
clean
mean(clean$stress, na.rm = TRUE)   # 3.5; with the 99 left in, it would be 22.6
```

(Base R's `startsWith()` and `tolower()` do the same job as stringr's `str_starts()` and `str_to_lower()` from the chapter.)
:::
:::
